newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Poor quality, low prices hit Vietnam coffee market.
newsitem.headline: Poor quality, low prices hit Vietnam coffee market.

text.p: A dive in London robusta futures to a 31-month low and lingering bean quality problems after heavy rains in the central highlands weighed on Vietnam's coffee market on Friday, traders said.

One trader said the benchmark January contract may test support at $1,325 a tonne after closing at $1,352 on Thursday, but thought a break of that level unlikely before the weekend because funds had already sold heavily and the U.S. market was closed.
"The price in London has dropped into hell," said another trader in Dak Lak province, Vietnam's main growing area, adding that a recovery was unlikely in the near future.
Vietnam's robusta export prices, although falling, have not yet matched London's losses. Traders put the market, FOB Saigon Port, at $1,060-1,080 a tonne compared with $1,100 a week ago.
"The Vietnamese market will have to follow at some time, they (sellers) will have to give in," said one trader. "They have a whole crop to sell."
Others noted quality problems for Vietnamese coffee because of heavy rains in the central highlands.
Excessive moisture has caused some beans to turn mouldy and that problem has been aggravated because the wet weather has delayed transport from the plantations to Saigon Port.
"Some buyers are complaining about quality," said one trader. "They say the beans are mouldy."
Traders said shipments had been very low for a November, roughly 15,000 tonnes compared with 26,000-30,000 in the same month last year.
Dak Lak province is responsible for up to two-thirds of Vietnam's total coffee output, which this season (Oct-Sept) is expected to reach 270,000 tonnes.
The Vietnam Economic Times journal, reporting this week on a recent coffee conference in Ho Chi Minh City, said that with a bumper crop ahead and low prices, many exporters were facing losses.

It quoted a senior official of the government pricing department as suggesting that an insurance system should be set up under which producers and traders would pay into a fund when prices were high and receive support when the market was weak.
